channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Effectiveness of a Personalized Robot-Assisted Trunk and Lower Limb Rehabilitation in Patients with Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: This RCT with 40 chronic stroke patients found that 3 months of personalized robot-assisted trunk and lower limb training, combined with conventional rehabilitation, significantly improved Functional Ambulatory Category (FAC) compared to conventional rehabilitation alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 articles explored the effectiveness and optimal dosage of physical exercise on cognitive function in older adults with Alzheimer's disease.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Foot-Targeted Rehabilitation for Pronation-Related Anterior Knee Pain: A Two-Phase Case-Control Study and Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Manual Therapy Versus Neuromuscular Training Each With Augmented Low-Dye Taping.
item.description: A two-phase study including an RCT compared foot-targeted physiotherapy for pronation-related anterior knee pain, finding that manual therapy with augmented low-dye taping and neuromuscular training with ALDT were both more effective than routine physiotherapy care in the short term.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of In-Clinic Rehabilitation vs. Home-Based Telerehabilitation for Adults with MS in the Deep South: The TEAMS Cluster Randomized Trial.
item.description: The TEAMS cluster randomized trial (n=759) found that a 12-week complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) program for multiple sclerosis delivered via home-based telerehabilitation was as effective as in-clinic rehabilitation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Optimal Exercise Modality and Dose for Blood Pressure Management in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Systematic Review with Bayesian Model-Based, and Dose-Response Network Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of RCTs found that for middle-aged and older adults, combined aerobic and resistance training, with sufficient volume, was most effective for lowering systolic and diastolic blood pressure, outperforming other modalities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of exercise-based prehabilitation before total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of RCTs comparing prehabilitation before total knee arthroplasty (TKA) found that multimodal exercise programs were more effective than single modalities, suggesting a comprehensive approach for better outcomes.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effects of combined balance and plyometric training on athletic performance: a systematic review
item.description: A systematic review found that combined balance and plyometric training significantly improves athletic performance, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing explosive power, agility, and dynamic stability for athletes.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effects of different aerobic exercise intensities on exercise capacity, quality of life and mortality in individuals with coronary artery disease: systematic review and network meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis found that moderate-intensity aerobic exercise may be the most effective for improving exercise capacity, quality of life, and mortality in individuals with coronary artery disease (CAD).
item.author: Sport Sci Health

item.title: Effectiveness of Telerehabilitation Versus Conventional Rehabilitation on Motor Function and Activities of Daily Living After Stroke: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of four RCTs (n=226) found telerehabilitation to be non-inferior to conventional physiotherapy for improving motor function (Fugl-Meyer Assessment) and activities of daily living (Barthel Index) in stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Body Acupuncture, Electroacupuncture, and Auricular Acupuncture in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs found acupuncture significantly improved motor function in stroke survivors compared to controls (SMD=6.48; 95% CI=4.72-8.24; P<0.001), with electroacupuncture showing the greatest efficacy among body, electro-, and auricular acupuncture.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness and feasibility of home-based physical exercise interventions for children and adolescents with chronic diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found home-based physical exercise interventions for children and adolescents with chronic diseases were effective in improving aerobic capacity, functional capacity, muscle strength, and quality of life, and were feasible, although reporting quality varied.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial with 50 patients found that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the elastic coefficient of the dermis in limb oedema compared to 0% tension taping by day 9, as measured by shear-wave elastography.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of six weeks of ankle stretching exercises on ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and anterior knee pain in children with ankle pronation: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that six weeks of ankle stretching exercises significantly improved ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and reduced anterior knee pain in children with ankle pronation.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Differences in the Thoracolumbar Fascia Between Low Back Pain Patients and Healthy Individuals: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis found differences in the thoracolumbar fascia (TLF) between low back pain patients and healthy individuals, suggesting the TLF plays a role in LBP and warrants further investigation into its pathophysiology and targeted interventions.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: The effect of SportsMetrics training program on functional performance, landing error, dynamic knee valgus and hamstrings/quadriceps strength in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that the SportsMetrics training program effectively improves functional performance, reduces landing errors and dynamic knee valgus, and enhances hamstring/quadriceps strength in athletes, supporting its role in injury prevention.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Sarcopenia among mid-to-older adults in Southeast Asia: A multi-national systematic review and meta-analysis of prevalence and risk factors
item.description: A multi-national systematic review and meta-analysis on sarcopenia in mid-to-older adults in Southeast Asia revealed high prevalence and identified key risk factors, underscoring the need for targeted interventions in the region.
item.author: Aging Clin Exp Res

item.title: Arm exercise training in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: An umbrella review synthesized evidence on arm exercise training for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), confirming its role as a component of pulmonary rehabilitation for managing extrapulmonary features.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Joint non-linear dose-response associations of device-measured physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness with cardiovascular disease: a cohort and Mendelian randomisation study
item.description: A UK Biobank cohort study with Mendelian randomization found a non-linear joint dose-response relationship between accelerometer-measured MVPA and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) with incident cardiovascular disease, showing greater benefits from combining both.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: More Than Just Arm Movement: Finger-Worn Accelerometers Provide a Valid and Sensitive Alternative to Wrist-Worn Accelerometers for Measuring Real-World Upper-Limb Performance in Stroke Survivors
item.description: A cross-sectional observational study of 20 stroke survivors demonstrated that finger-worn accelerometers provide a valid and sensitive alternative to wrist-worn accelerometers for measuring real-world upper-limb motor performance, capturing more nuanced movements.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effects of Fingertip Vibrotactile Stimulation on Postural Control in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Comparison Across Age Groups
item.description: A study with 348 community-dwelling older adults (aged 65-85+) found that fingertip vibrotactile stimulation affects postural control, with potential differences observed across young-old (65-74), old-old (75-84), and oldest-old (85+) age groups when standing with eyes closed.
item.author: medRxiv
